newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia 9-month trade gap narrows 12.9 pct/yr-ago.
newsitem.headline: Colombia 9-month trade gap narrows 12.9 pct/yr-ago.

text.p: Colombia's trade deficit narrowed 12.9 percent to $1.8 billion in the first nine months to September against the year-ago period, the National Statistics Department announced Tuesday.
From January to September, Colombia's exports increased 2.4 percent, mainly thanks to gains in coal and oil exports, while imports fell back 1.1 percent.
The trade deficit for the first nine months of the same period in 1995 was $2.07 billion, the department said in a statement issued Tuesday evening.

The value of Colombia's coal exports to September 1996 increased 58.6 percent. Volume was up 47.4 percent. Export revenue from crude oil rose 22 percent while the value of the export of oil derivatives increased 4 percent.
The volume of coffee exports rose 14.7 percent, but fell 15.1 percent in terms of value.

The value of non-traditional exports fell back 6.4 percent, largely on the back of a 66.45 percent fall in emerald export revenues and a drop of almost 30 percent in the value of exports of leather goods.
In the year to September, Colombia registered a trade surplus of $140.9 million with its Andean Pact partners, an increase of 60.3 percent.

The National Statistics Department also reported the trade deficit with France had dropped 61.1 percent, while the deficit with the United States fell 25 percent. This was offset by increases in the trade deficit with Spain and Mexico.
